title: Capital One Financial Corporation to Webcast Conference Call on Fourth Quarter 2025 Earnings
summary: MCLEAN, Va. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Dec. 19, 2025-- On Thursday, January 22, 2026 , at approximately 4:05 p.m. Eastern Time , Capital One Financial Corporation (NYSE: COF) will release its fourth quarter 2025 earnings results. Additionally, the company will host a conference call at 5:00 p.m.
body_text: MCLEAN, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Dec. 19, 2025-- On Thursday, January 22, 2026, at approximately 4:05 p.m. Eastern Time, Capital One Financial Corporation (NYSE: COF) will release its fourth quarter 2025 earnings results. Additionally, the company will host a conference call at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time to review financial and operating performance for the quarter ending December 31, 2025. The call will be webcast live and the earnings release will be available on the company’s homepage at www.capitalone.com . A replay of the webcast will be available 24 hours a day, beginning two hours after the conference call, until 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on February 5, 2026, through the company’s homepage. About Capital One Capital One Financial Corporation ( www.capitalone.com ) is a financial holding company which, along with its subsidiaries, had $468.8 billion in deposits and $661.9 billion in total assets as of September 30, 2025. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia, Capital One offers a broad spectrum of financial products and services to consumers, small businesses and commercial clients through a variety of channels. Capital One, N.A. has branches and Cafés located primarily in New York, Louisiana, Texas, Maryland, Virginia and the District of Columbia. A Fortune 500 company, Capital One trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “COF” and is included in the S&P 100 index. body_text: Norwood Financial Corp Announces Cash Dividend December 17, 2025 PDF Version HONESDALE, Pa., Dec. 17, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- James O. Donnelly, President and Chief Executive Officer of Norwood Financial Corp (NASDAQ Global Market - NWFL) and its subsidiary Wayne Bank, announced that the Board of Directors has declared a $0.32 per share cash dividend, which is payable on February 2, 2026, to shareholders of record as of January 15, 2026. The $0.32 per share is a $0.01 increase over the per share dividend declared in the fourth quarter of 2024. Mr. Donnelly commented, “The Board is extremely pleased to provide our shareholders with this quarterly dividend. It reflects the Company’s financial strength and strong capital position which has contributed to our solid performance.” Norwood Financial Corp, through its subsidiary, Wayne Bank operates fifteen offices in Northeastern Pennsylvania and fourteen offices in Delaware, Sullivan, Ontario, Otsego and Yates Counties, New York. As of September 30, 2025, Norwood had total assets of $2.412 billion, loans outstanding of $1.815 billion, total deposits of $2.074 billion and total capital of $234.9 million. The Company’s stock is traded on the Nasdaq Global Market under the symbol “NWFL”. Forward-Looking Statements . title: Bank account minimums are a scam: What to do instead
summary: This article might help you uncover an extra $3000, $5000, even $6000 to invest If you need to keep a minimum balance in your bank account, your money’s working for the bank, not you How I stopped paying banking fees (and kept more money for myself)
body_text: Highlights: This article might help you uncover an extra $3000, $5000, even $6000 to invest If you need to keep a minimum balance in your bank account, your money’s working for the bank, not you How I stopped paying banking fees (and kept more money for myself) “We have to keep at least $6,000 in our bank account at all times, or else we’ll get charged fees.” When my friend told me this, I was shocked . For one thing, there are the fees. I haven’t paid banking fees in 15 years. But the minimum balance is just as important. Nobody should have to tie up thousands of dollars just to do basic banking! We’re talking about why this isn’t great for your finances, what you can do instead. Why stay away from bank accounts that require minimum balances Your money is locked up These minimums are restrictive and affect how you use your own money. Dip below the threshold for even a day, and you could lose perks or get slapped with a fee. This can mess with your cash flow or force you to keep more in the account than you really need. Plus, many people need to keep thousands more in that account just so they have money to pull from. You could face unexpected fees It's not uncommon to be charged anywhere from $10 to $30 per month if your balance falls below the minimum - even temporarily. If that happens once a month, it could cost $360 a year just to hold your own money. No wonder banks are so great at turning a profit! If you continue using one of these accounts, at least set a notification when your balance gets low so you can top it up and don’t get dinged with fees. You’re missing out on better returns That $6,000 could be doing a lot more elsewhere: ✔️ Invested in a TFSA or RRSP for retirement ✔️ Earning 3-4% (or more) in a high-interest savings account ✔️ Paying down high-interest debt ✔️ Padding your emergency fund It gives a false sense of security Some people associate high minimums with higher quality service. But that doesn't always hold up. Many of these "premium" accounts offer the same support and worse interest rates than no-fee alternatives. You're not getting VIP treatment - you’re just keeping your money somewhere that helps the bank’s bottom line, not yours. You’re giving the bank a free loan Here’s the kicker… When you leave money in a low-yield bank account just to dodge a fee, you're giving the bank a free loan. As Vivian Tu shares in her video , “When you put money into a savings account, you’re essentially giving the bank a loan. They'll then turn around and lend that money out to people, and you better believe, they're charging those people interest.” In return? Traditional banks often pay you less than 0.1%. “If you put $100 into a savings account, at the end of the year, you'll have $100.06. ” “Wait, what? The bank is using my money?” Yes. Banks are smart. They know that they can use money to make more money. And with each client having thousands squirreled away in minimum bank balances, they have plenty at their disposal. How banks use your money to generate revenue Banks don’t keep your money sitting in a vault. They hold onto a small portion, and lend out the rest to make money from interest. This is called fractional reserve banking , and it’s how they earn a big chunk of their profits. When you keep a minimum balance in your account, you're basically giving them money they can lend out and generate interest from. “The Big Five” banks combined manage trillions of dollars. According to Investopedia , “Royal Bank of Canada recorded total net assets under management of $1.223 trillion. It also reported $6.6 billion of net interest income.” No wonder banks want us to park our money in their account! They’re earning billions from our dollars. You could be getting that interest instead! Let’s say you invest that $6,000 at 8% annual return. After 30 years, you’ll have over $60,000. That’s the magic of compound interest! Pretty great for not adding a penny more. What if you don’t maintain the minimum balance? You’re better off investing that money and paying the bank fees. In 30 years, you’ll pay over $10,000 in fees - but you'd still be $50,000 ahead thanks to your investments. That’s why high balances to save on fees are a false economy: in reality, you’re losing out. You’d make much more if your money were invested. So you’ve got 3 opinions: 1: Stay with the bank, maintain the minimum balance, and save $10,000 2: Stay with the bank, pay the fees, invest the minimum balance, and be ahead by $50,000 in retirement 3: Switch to a no-fee bank, invest what was previously your minimum balance, and be ahead by $60,000 in retirement! Ready for free banking? Try these! Choose a new bank There are so many good options out there now, you can definitely find a bank that doesn’t require you to stash thousands of dollars simply for the privilege of banking with them. Plus, you can often get better interest rates on high-interest savings accounts! Here are some options to check out: Tangerine Simplii EQ bank KOHO Use a credit union I banked for free with a credit union for years . Of course, check the fine print - some have fees like traditional banks, but many offer free banking. Negotiate In some cases, keeping your account at a traditional bank still makes sense. For example, we have a mortgage through National Bank - and they require us to have an account. However, we negotiated to have them cover all the banking fees (normally $28.95 a month). We’ve had this account for almost 9 years now, and haven’t paid a penny in fees - or kept a minimum balance. Bye, bank! Use a bank that works for you There are so many no-fee banks out there with services that are comparable to the big banks. Many now offer services that traditional banks offer, or even charge for - like debit cards, ATM usage, and Interac transfers. Setting up a new account can take as little as 10 minutes! Once you no longer need to keep a minimum balance, you have more money to invest! And if you want to make investing easy, Passiv is exactly what you need to stay on track with your goals. It connects to your brokerage account, lets you build a target portfolio, and keeps everything balanced. Use the “Forever Free” plan , and never use spreadsheets to manage your investments again! title: GATX Corporation and Brookfield Infrastructure Receive All Required Regulatory Clearances to Complete the Acquisition of Wells Fargo’s Rail Assets
summary: GATX Corporation (NYSE: GATX) today announced that it, together with Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. (“BIP”) (NYSE: BIP; TSX: BIP.UN) and its institutional partners (collectively, “Brookfield Infrastructure”), has received all required regulatory clearances to complete the transaction to acquire Wells Fargo’s rail operating lease portfolio. title: Celularity CEO Comments on Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services’ Withdrawal of Skin Substitute Local Coverage Determinations
body_text: Celularity CEO Comments on Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services’ Withdrawal of Skin Substitute Local Coverage Determinations By Celularity Inc. in Press Releases While Celularity’s Biovance® and Biovance 3L products remained eligible for Medicare coverage under the now-withdrawn LCDs, Celularity CEO Dr. Robert J. Hariri welcomed the recent action taken under the leadership of CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz FLORHAM PARK, N.J., Dec. 26, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Celularity Inc. (Nasdaq: CELU) (“Celularity”), a regenerative and cellular medicine company addressing age-related and degenerative diseases, today released comments by Robert J. Hariri, M.D., Ph.D., CEO and Chairman, on the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services’ (CMS) recent withdrawal of skin substitute Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) that were set to go into effect on January 1, 2026. On December 24, 2025, CMS announced that effective immediately, A/B Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs) were withdrawing the LCDs for Skin Substitute Grafts/Cellular and Tissue-Based Products for the Treatment of Diabetic Foot Ulcers and Venous Leg Ulcers scheduled to become effective on January 1, 2026. The LCDs, adopted under an earlier Medicare 2026 Skin Substitute Update, set which skin substitute products would be eligible for Medicare coverage beginning in 2026. While Celularity’s Biovance® and Biovance 3L remained eligible for Medicare coverage under the now-withdrawn LCDs, Medicare coverage was eliminated for 158 skin substitute products sold by other companies. Unaffected by CMS’ recent action is its new payment policy that effective January 1, 2026, all skin substitute applications furnished in physician office settings and hospital outpatient department settings will be paid at a flat rate of $127.28 per square centimeter. Commenting on the recent change, Dr. Hariri said, “We have amassed substantial real-world evidence, or RWE, from multiple studies showing how our Biovance® Human Amniotic Membrane Allograft works in actual clinical practice for wound healing, demonstrating its effectiveness in diverse, real-life diverse patient populations patients with chronic wounds. RWE from large observational studies published in the peer-reviewed journal WOUNDS and elsewhere show Biovance® effectively treats chronic wounds, even in patients with multiple health issues. Other RWE shows reduced steroid use in about half of patients treated with Biovance®, which evidence indicates helps decrease pro-inflammatory factors and increase anti-inflammatory ones, guiding the body’s natural healing.” Dr. Hariri noted that CMS’ 2026 Medicare payment policy setting skin substitute reimbursement at a flat $127.28 per square centimeter remains in effect despite it withdrawing the LCDs. “Biovance® has been supported by a highly efficient, proven scalable manufacturing process since its commercial launch in April 2014, which today allows us to operate comfortably under the new Medicare reimbursement for skin substitute products,” he said. “Our sustained investment in advanced infrastructure includes a world-class GMP/GTP manufacturing facility located in Florham Park, New Jersey, where today we manufacture a range of commercial advanced biomaterial products and investigational cell therapy products, including both Celularity branded products and contract manufactured products for third parties. Consistent with our emphasis on real-world evidence gained from actual clinical use of our products, we have integrated an ‘Industry 5.0’ approach into our manufacturing operations, introducing digitization and AI and building adaptable and robust value chains and production systems,” Dr. Hariri said. About Celularity Celularity Inc. (Nasdaq: CELU) is a regenerative and aging-related cellular medicine company developing, manufacturing, and commercializing advanced biomaterial products and allogeneic and autologous cell therapies, all derived from the postpartum placenta. Celularity believes that by harnessing the placenta’s unique biology and ready availability, it can develop therapeutic solutions that address significant unmet global needs for effective, accessible, and affordable therapies that target fundamental aging mechanisms like cellular senescence, age-related chronic inflammation, and tissue degeneration. For more information about Celularity and its cutting-edge regenerative medicine solutions, please visit www.celularity.com. title: Adicet Bio Announces Reverse Stock Split
summary: REDWOOD CITY, Calif. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Dec. 26, 2025-- Adicet Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq: ACET), a clinical stage biotechnology company discovering and developing allogeneic gamma delta T cell therapies for autoimmune diseases and cancer, today announced that its board of directors has determined to effect
body_text: Investors Press Release Details Adicet Bio Announces Reverse Stock Split December 26, 2025 at 8:30 AM EST PDF Version REDWOOD CITY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Dec. 26, 2025-- Adicet Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq: ACET), a clinical stage biotechnology company discovering and developing allogeneic gamma delta T cell therapies for autoimmune diseases and cancer, today announced that its board of directors has determined to effect a one-for-16 reverse stock split of Adicet’s common stock, par value $0.0001 per share. The reverse stock split ratio approved by the board of directors is within the previously disclosed range of ratios for a reverse stock split authorized by the stockholders of the company at the 2025 Special Meeting of Stockholders of Adicet held on December 19, 2025. The reverse stock split will take effect at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on December 30, 2025, and Adicet’s common stock will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis on The Nasdaq Capital Market as of the opening of trading on December 30, 2025. The CUSIP number of 007002207 will be assigned to Adicet’s common stock when the reverse stock split becomes effective. When the reverse stock split becomes effective, every sixteen (16) of Adicet’s issued shares of common stock will be combined into one issued share of common stock, without any change to the par value per share. This will reduce the number of outstanding shares of common stock from approximately 153.3 million shares to approximately 9.6 million shares. The reverse stock split will not affect the absolute number of Adicet’s authorized shares of common stock, which will remain at 300,000,000, but the total number of shares of Adicet’s common stock available for future issuance will increase. Proportional adjustments will also be made to the number of shares of common stock awarded and available for issuance under Adicet’s equity incentive plans, as well as the exercise price and the number of shares issuable upon the exercise or conversion of Adicet’s outstanding stock options and other equity securities under Adicet’s equity incentive plans. All outstanding pre-funded warrants will also be adjusted in accordance with their terms, which will result in proportionate adjustments being made to the number of shares issuable upon exercise of such warrants and to the exercise prices of such warrants, as applicable. No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the reverse stock split. Stockholders who would otherwise be entitled to receive fractional shares will automatically be entitled to receive cash in lieu of such fractional share. Stockholders with shares held in book-entry form or through a bank, broker, or other nominee are not required to take any action and will see the consequence of the reverse stock split reflected in their accounts on or after December 30, 2025. Such beneficial holders may contact their bank, broker, or nominee for more information. The reverse stock split is intended to enable Adicet to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market. About Adicet Bio, Inc. Adicet Bio, Inc. is a clinical stage biotechnology company discovering and developing allogeneic gamma delta T cell therapies for autoimmune diseases and cancer. Adicet is advancing a pipeline of “off-the-shelf” gamma delta T cells, engineered with chimeric antigen receptors (CARs), to facilitate durable activity in patients. For more information, please visit our website at https://www.adicetbio.com . title: 7 Hindi phrases to know before travelling to India
summary: Learn key Hindi phrases and local culture to make your digital nomad life easier while working remotely from India.
body_text: Living in India as a digital nomad can feel exciting and overwhelming at the same time. The colours, the noise, the pace, everything moves fast, and English won’t always carry you through daily life. Learning a few key phrases can make all the difference. You can order food with confidence, navigate daily life smoothly, and connect beyond your laptop screen. This guide shows you how speaking some Hindi can help, plus cultural tips that help you settle in, feel comfortable, and truly enjoy your stay in India. Also read: How Indians abroad light up the world during Diwali. Why digital nomads should learn basic Hindi When you arrive in India as a digital nomad, everyday life moves quickly. Knowing a few local phrases can change how you experience the country, helping you feel more confident, connected, and at ease. Easier communication When you know basic Hindi phrases, simple tasks become smoother. Ordering food, asking for directions, or negotiating prices feels less stressful. You don’t rely entirely on translation apps, and locals often respond more patiently and warmly when you try to speak their language. Cultural integration Using key phrases shows respect for local culture. Even small efforts help you blend in, understand social cues, and avoid awkward moments. You stop feeling like a visitor and start feeling part of everyday life around you. Building relationships Speaking a little Hindi opens doors to real conversations. Shop owners, neighbours, and colleagues become more approachable. Those small exchanges often turn into friendships, recommendations, and deeper connections that make your stay more meaningful. Also read: How Indian freelancers are adapting to global payment trends Hindi phrases every digital nomad should know in India. Living in India gets a lot easier when you know a few Hindi phrases. You don’t need to be fluent, just confident enough to greet, ask, and respond naturally. These basics will help you move through daily life with ease. Namaste (नमस्ते) – Hello This is the safest and most respectful way to greet anyone in India. You can use it in shops, offices, cafés, or when meeting someone new. Pair it with a smile or folded hands, and you instantly come across as polite. Try saying, “Namaste! Aap kaise hain?” (Hello! How are you?). It’s polite, safe, and always appreciated. Dhanyavaad / Shukriya (धन्यवाद / शुक्रिया) – Thank you Gratitude goes a long way in India. Saying “Dhanyavaad or Shukriya” shows appreciation and respect, whether someone gives directions or helps you at work. Even if the rest of your sentence is in English, adding this word softens interactions. For example, “Dhanyavaad aapki madad ke liye!” (Thank you for your help). Even one word changes how people respond to you. Haan / Nahi (हाँ / नहीं) – Yes / No These two words will be some of the most useful you learn. You’ll use them when ordering food, answering questions, or confirming plans. Locals expect quick, clear responses, and using haan or nahi avoids confusion. You’ll hear questions constantly. Example: “Chai chahiye?” (Do you want tea?)You answer: “Haan.” (Yes) or “Nahi.” (No) Simple, direct, and much clearer than nodding or guessing. Kripya / Meherbani karke (कृपया / मेहरबानी करके) – Please Politeness matters, and these words help you ask for things respectfully. Use kripya in formal situations and meherbani karke casually. Even simple requests sound better this way. Saying, “Kripya mujhe ek bottle paani dijiye.” (Please give me a bottle of water.) softens your request and makes interactions smoother, especially with locals. Aap kaise hain? (आप कैसे हैं?) – How are you? This is a friendly way to start conversations and show interest. It works with colleagues, neighbours, or shop owners. Asking how someone is often leads to small talk, smiles, and better interactions. It’s simple, polite, and makes you feel less like an outsider from the start. Example: “Namaste, aap kaise hain?” You'll often hear: “Main theek hoon.” (I’m fine.)It opens doors to friendly small talk. Mujhe madad chahiye (मुझे मदद चाहिए) – I need help This phrase is important when you’re lost, confused, or need assistance. People are generally willing to help once they understand you need it. Saying “Mujhe madad chahiye” clearly communicates urgency without panic. It’s especially useful with drivers, shopkeepers, or locals nearby. Example: “Mujhe madad chahiye, main rasta bhool gaya hoon.” (I need help, I’m lost.)Ye kitne ka hai? (यह कितने का है?) – How much is this? You’ll use this almost daily in markets and local shops. Asking in Hindi shows confidence and often leads to friendlier prices. Point to the item and say the phrase clearly. Even if bargaining follows in English, starting in Hindi sets the tone for smoother interactions. Also read: How freelancers in India can invoice clients abroad easily. Cultural tips for nomads living in India Living and working in India goes beyond Wi-Fi and workspaces. Understanding a few cultural habits helps you blend in, avoid awkward moments, and build respectful connections wherever you choose to stay. Greetings When you meet people, especially elders, greeting them with Namaste and folded hands shows respect. As a digital nomad, this small gesture helps you make a good first impression in homes, offices, and local communities, even if the rest of the conversation happens in English. Hands In India, your right hand is used for giving, receiving, and eating. As a nomad, being mindful of this shows cultural awareness in daily interactions, from paying for food to sharing items. It’s a simple habit that quickly earns respect and avoids uncomfortable moments. Footwear Removing your shoes before entering homes, temples, or mosques is expected. As a remote worker moving between spaces, always look for shoes at the door as a cue. Following this practice shows respect and helps you feel more comfortable in local environments. Dress code Dressing modestly, especially in religious places, is important. As a digital nomad, choosing clothing that covers shoulders and knees helps you blend in, avoid unwanted attention, and show cultural sensitivity while exploring cities, towns, and sacred spaces. But remote life isn’t complete without smooth payments. You need a way to receive your money on time, without losses from slow transfers or poor exchange rates. title: We Compared AI SDR and Sales Agent Tools So You Don’t Have to
summary: See how six leading AI SDR tools stack up on cost, features, and fit—so your team sells smarter, not just faster.
body_text: ‍ TL;DR 1 The AI SDR category split in 2026. Inbound is dominated by Qualified (Piper) with a $70K–$128K/year total cost including required Salesforce. Outbound is crowded, with 11x, Artisan, and Regie fighting on price and speed of deployment. Signal-based prospecting (Factors) sits in its own lane. Founder-led teams asking “which AI SDR should I use?” are usually asking the wrong question, and the honest answer is often “none of them, yet.” 2 Chloe , the AI sales agent built into Close, went generally available in June 2026 across all Close plans (Solo, Essentials, Growth, Scale). Chloe is not a standalone AI SDR seat. It is an agent inside the AI-native CRM that transcribes calls, drafts follow-ups, updates records, and can place outbound calls on US and Canadian numbers in English. That design difference matters more than the feature list. 3 Do not buy an AI SDR before you fix your speed-to-lead problem. In beta, teams using Chloe cut median first-touch time on inbound leads by more than half. A calling-first CRM plus one AI teammate outperforms three separate SDR bots for teams under 10 reps in nearly every scenario we tested. 4 The reputational risk on some 2026 vendors is real. Public reports on Artisan and 11x include zero-response campaigns, hallucinated customer news, and disputed logos. Read the reviews before you sign anything annual. The state of AI SDR tools in June 2026 The AI SDR category is a year and a half old and already unrecognizable from where it started. New entrants launched, funding rounds hit the press, and a handful of well-funded vendors picked up loud criticism from actual buyers. Our own AI sales agent, Chloe , went generally available in June 2026, which gives us first-party data on 306 businesses and 818,000-plus calls to compare against the standalone SDR bots. This is the honest read on what we would tell a founder asking "which AI SDR should I use" today. If you want to skip the reading, start a free 14-day trial of Close (no credit card) and see Chloe in action inside your own workspace. Otherwise, keep going. The AI SDR category in June 2026, honestly "AI SDR" is not a product category. It is a marketing term that got applied to at least four different types of software. Grouping them together is how buyers end up with the wrong tool. Type one is inbound conversational AI. Piper from Qualified is the mature example. It engages website visitors in real time via chat, voice, and video, then hands qualified leads to a human. Type two is outbound agent-as-a-service. Ava from Artisan and Alice/Jordan from 11x sit here. You buy an AI seat, feed it an ICP and a domain, and it sends thousands of cold emails and (sometimes) cold calls. Type three is signal-based prospecting. Factors.ai identifies which accounts are showing buying intent so a human rep can act on that signal. It is not really an SDR at all, but it keeps getting compared to them. Type four is embedded AI teammate. Chloe from Close fits here, along with the built-in AI layers in HubSpot's Sales Hub and Salesforce Agentforce. These agents live inside your CRM and handle work you were already doing, rather than replacing a human seat. Each type solves a different problem. Buying the wrong type is expensive. We will walk through all four with real pricing and honest limits. The eight-tool comparison at a glance Tool Best for Type Starting price Contract Key limit Close (Chloe) Founder-led teams under 10 reps who need calling plus AI in one place Embedded AI teammate $9–$139/user/mo (annual) Monthly or annual US/CA numbers, English only at launch Qualified (Piper) Enterprise inbound with Salesforce already in place Inbound conversational AI ~$40K–$68K/yr (25 users) Annual Requires Salesforce; inbound only 11x (Alice/Jordan) Enterprise outbound volume where budget is not the issue Outbound agent-as-a-service ~$40K–$60K/yr per agent Annual, quarterly break Public churn and hallucination reports Artisan (Ava) Teams that want a single AI outbound seat Outbound agent-as-a-service ~$2K/mo, annual only Annual Frequent 0-star reviews on quality Regie.ai Mid-market outbound with an existing SEP motion Outbound agent + enrichment $180/user/mo (10 seat min) Annual $21.6K/yr floor; enterprise-shaped AiSDR Small teams testing AI outbound quarterly Outbound agent-as-a-service $900/mo (quarterly) Quarterly, min 3 months 1,200 messages/mo at Explore tier Factors.ai Marketing teams needing intent signals for sales Signal-based prospecting $399/mo (annual) Annual Not an SDR; needs sales team to act MarketOwl Solo founders testing LinkedIn outbound LinkedIn/email outbound agent $300–$500/mo per campaign Monthly or annual One LinkedIn profile per campaign Pricing verified June 2026 against each vendor's public pricing page or, where pricing is quote-only, against multiple independent buyer reports. See Sources for links. Before you pick a tool, run the speed-to-lead math The single biggest driver of pipeline lift from AI SDR tooling is not "more messages sent." It is faster first response on inbound leads that already came to you. Harvard Business Review has cited this for years. Teams that respond within 5 minutes are 21 times more likely to qualify the lead than teams that wait 30 minutes. In our own Chloe beta with 306 businesses across 818,000-plus calls, the median first-touch time dropped by more than half once outbound and inbound work lived in the same CRM as the AI agent. If your median inbound first-touch is under 10 minutes and your outbound is already running, an AI SDR is a scale lever. If your median is 30 minutes or more, buying an AI outbound seat is like buying a bigger sink when the drain is clogged. Fix the drain first. You can test this yourself with a 14-day trial of Close and a live inbound form. Start the trial here . Tool-by-tool honest read 1. Close (Chloe): the embedded AI teammate We are the makers of Close, so read this section with that in mind. Chloe is the AI sales agent built into Close. She went generally available in June 2026 across every Close plan (Solo, Essentials, Growth, and Scale). Chloe is not sold as a separate SDR seat. She is an agent that lives inside the AI-native CRM you already use to place calls, send email, and manage deals. What Chloe actually does: transcribes and summarizes every call, drafts follow-up emails from those transcripts for human review, handles prospect enrichment as calls happen, flags stalled deals, and places outbound calls on US and Canadian phone numbers in English at launch. Every AI call opens with a required disclosure that it is an AI and that the call is recorded. That is a compliance choice, not a limitation. Chloe is not a magic outbound machine. She does not spray 10,000 emails a week. She is designed to lift the ceiling on what a small team can do without adding headcount, not to replace the team. Beta results for named customers include FollowUp.com booking 50% more qualified appointments and Flatiron School running admissions outreach at higher call volume with the same counselors. Chloe pairs with Close's native Power Dialer for outbound-heavy teams that want AI notes and follow-up drafts sitting in the deal by the time they hang up. Full context is on the Chloe launch post . Pricing is transparent, on our pricing page : Solo $9, Essentials $35, Growth $99, and Scale $139 per user per month on annual billing. Chloe usage is metered through AI credits plus standard telephony costs, so a small team pays for what it actually uses instead of a flat AI seat fee. New Close customers can use code CHLOEPARTNER30 for 30% off the first three months (through June 30, 2026). Best fit: founder-led teams under 10 reps running both inbound and outbound in the same week. Weak fit: enterprise inbound programs already deep in Salesforce (see Qualified below) and non-English outbound at launch. 2. Qualified (Piper): the inbound heavyweight Piper is the most mature product in the category, with ~4.9 / 5 across 1,487 G2 reviews as of June 2026 (the highest rating in the conversational marketing category). Piper engages website visitors in real time via chat, voice, and video, qualifies them, books meetings on real reps' calendars, and hands warm handoffs to Salesforce. It works. It also costs six figures once you add the required Salesforce stack. Pricing is quote-only. Based on Vendr negotiation data and multiple public buyer reports, Qualified Premier lists around $68,000 per year for 25 users and negotiates to roughly $40,000–$50,000. Salesforce CRM is required (no exceptions), adding $30,000–$60,000 per year for a 10-seat team, plus intent data and implementation. Enterprise deployments run anywhere from $50,000 to $500,000+ per year depending on tier. In Q2 2026, Qualified announced PiperX, a multi-modal upgrade with cross-channel engagement and deeper CRM integration. If you are already on Salesforce and your inbound pipeline is the bottleneck, Piper is the gold standard. If you are on HubSpot, Pipedrive, or Close, you cannot use Qualified at all. If you are outbound-heavy, Piper does not cover that motion. For teams weighing the underlying CRM decision itself, our speed benchmarks against Salesforce, HubSpot, and Pipedrive cover how the platform choice affects rep throughput. 3. 11x (Alice and Jordan): read the coverage before you sign 11x sells Alice for outbound (email, LinkedIn) and Julian/Jordan for inbound voice. Pricing is quote-only. Vendr median deal size is $40,125 per year. Public reports put Alice at roughly $50,000 to $60,000 per year, with the Jordan voice add-on in the $50,000-plus range. G2 sits at 4.5 / 5 across ~10 reviews , a small sample size worth weighing against the coverage below. This is the part where we would normally list features. Instead, we are going to link the coverage. In March 2025, TechCrunch reported that 11x had displayed customer logos, including ZoomInfo and Airtable, for companies that were not customers. ZoomInfo issued a cease-and-desist. The story also cited claims of $10M ARR against actual figures closer to $3M, and reported that the company was seeing high churn within a three-month break clause. In Q2 2026, 11x brought in a new CEO, Prabhav Jain, and has been rebuilding the product and go-to-market story. Multiple buyer forums continue to report churn rates in the 70–75% range within the first three months, though 11x disputes these figures. We do not have a position on whether 11x is fixed under the new CEO. We do have a position on signing a $50,000 annual contract for outbound email that you can accomplish for a fraction of the cost with a well-configured stack. If you evaluate 11x, ask for named customer references you can call, verify the logos on the website, and read the current coverage before you commit. 4. Artisan (Ava): the reputation problem Ava is Artisan's outbound AI SDR. Pricing runs around $2,000 per month on annual-only contracts. Artisan raised significant funding and put its brand on Bay Area billboards with a provocative "Stop hiring humans" campaign in 2024. The buyer feedback is where things get uncomfortable. As of mid-2026, public writeups collecting Artisan reviews point to zero-star G2 ratings citing brand damage and "extremely bland and obviously AI" copy, Hacker News threads reporting 0% effective response rates and hallucinated fake company news in outbound emails, Reddit posts describing 1,400 emails sent with zero responses, and multiple buyers reporting difficulty canceling contracts. Gizmodo and other outlets have written about Artisan as an example of "software to automate spamming." We are not saying Artisan cannot work for anyone. We are saying that if you are considering a $24,000-per-year annual contract, you should read the current coverage first and demand named customer references before you sign. The category has better options. 5. Regie.ai: enterprise pricing, mid-market pain point Regie sells an AI SEP (sales engagement platform) at $180 per user per month with a 10-seat minimum ($21,600 per year floor) and a Force Multiplier Rep tier at $499 per user per month with a five-seat minimum ($29,940 per year floor). Add-ons include a Parallel Dialer at $1,800 per user per year and mailbox rotation at $50–$100 per user per month. The product includes a 220M-plus contact database and 339 G2 reviews as of June 2026. Regie is a reasonable pick if you already have an SEP motion (Outreach, Salesloft) and want to add an AI generation layer on top. It is a bad pick if you are a five-person team looking for a first outbound tool, because the seat minimums put you at $22,000 to $30,000 per year before you know whether the motion works. 6. AiSDR: the quarterly-billing option AiSDR sells two plans plus custom enterprise. Explore is $900 per month billed quarterly ($2,700 upfront, or $8,640 per year on annual). Grow is $2,500 per month quarterly ($7,500 upfront, $24,000 annual). Explore includes 1,200 AI-generated messages and 1,200 lead search credits per month. G2 sits at ~4.7 / 5 across ~76 reviews as of early 2026. The quarterly billing is the honest differentiator. If you want to test AI outbound for 90 days without committing to a full year, AiSDR is the shortest commitment window in the outbound-agent category. Expected output on Explore, per AiSDR's own projections, is around 3 meetings per month, which comes out to roughly $300 per meeting booked. Whether that math works depends on your deal size and close rate. Below a $10K ACV, it usually does not. 7. Factors.ai: intent signals, not an SDR Factors.ai identifies which accounts are showing buying intent by combining anonymous website visitor de-anonymization, LinkedIn signals, G2 engagement, and CRM data. It scores accounts so a human rep knows who to call. It does not send messages or place calls. Pricing (verified June 2026): Free tier covers 200 companies per month. Basic is $399 per month ($4,788 per year) for 3,000 companies. Growth is $999 per month for 8,000 companies. Enterprise is custom, typically $25K–$30K per year. Add-ons are where costs balloon: LinkedIn AdPilot is $1,000 per month, Interest Groups is $750 per month. A Basic plan with both add-ons is $2,149 per month, not $399. G2 sits at 4.5 / 5 across ~179 reviews . Best fit: marketing teams running ABM with a rep team ready to act on the signals. Weak fit: teams expecting Factors to do the outbound work itself. It will not. 8. MarketOwl: the LinkedIn-first budget option MarketOwl runs autonomous LinkedIn plus email outbound campaigns tied to one LinkedIn profile per campaign. Pricing is $500 per month per campaign on monthly, or $300 per month with a 12-month commitment. An "AI SDR + AI SMM" bundle is $329 per month with a one-year commitment. Free-form trial available. MarketOwl is the cheapest option in this comparison and it is aimed at solo founders and one-person sales teams testing outbound. It is not a serious competitor to Chloe, Piper, or Regie for teams with even three reps, but it does what it says on the label at a price a bootstrapped founder can absorb for one quarter of testing. Our honest recommendations by team shape The right AI SDR depends more on your team shape than on the vendor's feature list. Here is how we actually advise founders when they ask. Solo founder or 1–3 person team, mixed inbound and outbound. Skip the standalone AI SDR bots. Get a calling-first CRM with an embedded AI teammate. Close with Chloe is the cleanest fit . If you want a lighter-weight LinkedIn-only motion for one quarter, MarketOwl at $300/month is a reasonable test. Founder-led team, 4–10 reps, outbound-heavy. Same recommendation, with the outbound motion moved into Power Dialer and Chloe handling call summaries and follow-up drafts. This is the profile where Chloe's design center pays off most, because the after-call ritual for 10 reps compounds into hours per day of admin that Chloe removes. If you are ready to compare Close's plan tiers, the Growth plan at $99/user/mo is where most teams in this profile land. Marketing-led inbound engine already running on Salesforce, 20+ reps. Qualified with Piper is the right tool. Yes, the total cost of ownership is $70K–$128K per year. If your inbound pipeline is worth several million in ARR, the math works. It also stacks well with signal-based prospecting like Factors.ai. If you are on any CRM other than Salesforce, this recommendation does not apply. See our Pipedrive comparison and other CRM comparisons for the right alternative. Mid-market outbound team with a mature SEP motion, 15+ reps. Regie.ai is the most defensible pick, provided you already have Outreach or Salesloft in place. If you do not, do not buy Regie as your first outbound tool. Buy a CRM with native outbound first, then layer AI on top when you know the motion works. Enterprise outbound, budget is not the constraint. We would still not recommend 11x or Artisan without reading the current coverage and demanding named customer references you can call. If those check out for your specific use case, fine. If they do not, the enterprise outbound category is not actually mature enough yet to justify a $50K-plus annual seat. Two shifts worth watching in the next six months The category is moving fast enough that a comparison written today has a short shelf life. Two shifts are worth watching before your next AI SDR evaluation. The reputational read on 11x is unsettled. TechCrunch's reporting on disputed customer logos and the gap between publicly claimed and actual ARR is the reason 11x sits neutral-to-cautious on our list. New CEO Prabhav Jain took over in Q2 2026, and the product and go-to-market story is being rebuilt. If you are evaluating 11x, weigh the current buyer reports against whatever the sales team tells you, and ask for named customer references you can call. Standard due diligence for any AI sales tool at this price point . The embedded-agent model is pulling ahead of the standalone-agent model for small teams. Chloe's first six months of production data across 306 businesses and 818,000-plus calls point to consistently better outcomes for teams under 10 reps compared to bolting a separate SDR bot onto a legacy CRM. Bigger teams and inbound-heavy motions are a different story (Qualified still wins that segment), but the small-team default has shifted. Expect HubSpot and Salesforce to lean harder into their own embedded agents through the back half of 2026. "Most 'we need an AI SDR' conversations from founder-led teams are actually 'we need faster first-touch on inbound and a shorter after-call ritual.' Buy the tool that solves that." Get the weekly take We publish Dialed In , a weekly newsletter with sales fuel worth actually reading. We cover new AI SDR launches, pricing changes, and honest buyer reports as they happen. Subscribe from any page on close.com . Dialed In WEEKLY Weekly sales fuel in your inbox . Thank you! You're subscribed. Oops! Something went wrong while submitting the form. ‍ Where to start tomorrow Before you evaluate any AI SDR tool, run three quick checks against your own team. One, measure your current median time to first human touch on inbound leads. Pull last month's form fills and time the gap. If it is over 15 minutes, no AI SDR will fix that. Speed-to-lead is a CRM problem , not an outbound-agent problem. Two, count your current sales stack. If you already have a dialer, a sequencer, a notetaker, an enrichment tool , and a CRM, adding an AI SDR seat on top will not help. Consolidation almost always beats addition. A single CRM plus email plus calling plus SMS workspace is the cleanest setup for teams under 10 reps. Three, sit with a rep for one day and time the after-call ritual. If it is over five minutes per call, an embedded AI teammate is the highest-leverage change you can make. Native calling with AI notes collapses that ritual to under 90 seconds in the workflows we have measured. For more on the broader category, see our companion pieces on the best AI outreach tools , 13 AI sales tools we tested , and whether AI SDRs actually work . If any of that sounds familiar, start a free 14-day trial of Close and see whether Chloe fits your motion before you spend $50K on an outbound agent seat elsewhere. ‍ ‍

body_text: View All News Perma-Pipe International Holdings, Inc. Announces the Appointment of Richard Sherrill to its Board of Directors 12/05/2025 Download (opens in new window) THE WOODLANDS, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Perma-Pipe International Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: PPIH), today announced changes to its Board of Directors (the "Board"), including the appointment of Richard M. Sherrill to the Board, effective immediately. Mr. Sherrill, 59, has served as a member of the Board of Talos Energy, Inc. ("Talos"; NYSE: TALO) since February 2023, an upstream oil and natural gas exploration company. Mr. Sherrill also serves as the Senior Vice President of Business Development for Howard Energy Partners, a private midstream energy infrastructure company. From 2003 to 2019, Mr. Sherrill was the President and a board member of Ceritas Energy LLC, a midstream infrastructure company focused on midstream gathering and process solutions in various onshore regions of the United States of America and backed by private equity firms Quantum Energy Partners and Energy Spectrum Partners and was a founder of the company in 2003. From 1999 to 2003, Mr. Sherrill held various senior management roles at Duke Energy Corporation, which led to his appointment as Chief Operating Officer over the company's North American commercial activities in the deregulated natural gas and power space. From 1992 to 1999, Mr. Sherrill served in various capacities for Dynegy, Inc. Prior thereto, Mr. Sherrill began his career with First Interstate Bank of Texas, now a part of Wells Fargo, serving upstream, midstream, and energy merchant clients as a component of the firm's Energy Lending Group. Mr. Sherrill graduated from the University of Texas at Austin in 1988 with a Bachelor of Business Administration degree in finance. Chairman of the Board, Mr. Jon Biro commented, "Mr. Sherrill brings an exceptional record of business leadership and extensive industry expertise, and I welcome him to the Board. He will assume the Board seat previously held by Mr. Rob McNally, and we extend our sincere appreciation to Mr. McNally for his service and contributions." President and CEO, Mr. Saleh Sagr commented, "Mr. Sherrill's appointment as an Independent Director will meaningfully enhance the Board's strategic depth and provide invaluable insight as the Company advances its ambitious growth agenda. I also thank Mr. McNally for his service and contributions as a member of our Board and wish him well in his future endeavors. Perma-Pipe International Holdings, Inc. Perma-Pipe International Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: PPIH, “Perma-Pipe”, or the “Company”) is a global leader in pre-insulated piping and leak detection systems for oil and gas, district heating and cooling, and other applications. It uses its extensive engineering and fabrication expertise to develop piping solutions that solve complex challenges regarding the safe and efficient transportation of many types of liquids. In total, Perma-Pipe has operations at fourteen locations in seven countries. These statements should be considered as subject to the many risks and uncertainties that exist in the Company's operations and business environment. Such risks and uncertainties include, but are not limited to, the following: (i) fluctuations in the price of oil and natural gas and its impact on customer order volume for the Company's products; (ii) the Company’s ability to purchase raw materials at favorable prices and to maintain beneficial relationships with its suppliers;
